behaved.label: Handed to Charlie
behaved.why: Reached Staff through Alpha and handed to Charlie at 10s.
behaved.tip: Staff picked up and the check was handed to Charlie. Nobody answering is not his fault; our own side never handing him the check is.
behaved.rule: Mapping talks to machines, Charlie talks to people: nothing in mapping ever speaks to a person.

behaved.label: The question played as a recording
behaved.why: The question played as a recording at 6s.
behaved.tip: The question is played from our own recording, so asking it costs nothing. Charlie asking it himself works, and costs more.
behaved.rule: Delta asks the question from a recording; Charlie never asks it again in any wording.

behaved.label: Charlie warmed up in time
behaved.tip: Charlie starts connecting two seconds before the recorded question ends, so he is ready the moment it finishes. Late means Staff heard silence.
behaved.rule: Charlie warms up behind the recording so he is ready the moment the question ends.

behaved.label: We reached the right department
behaved.why: This check never picked a department.
behaved.tip: Only counts on a check that picked a department. Landing somewhere that cannot answer is not a fault; not asking to be put through is.
behaved.rule: If Staff cannot answer, ask ONCE, warmly, to be put through. Never ask a second time on a check.

behaved.label: Asked to be transferred
behaved.why: No wrong department reached. No transfer needed.
behaved.tip: Only counts when Staff said we reached the wrong department. Charlie must then request a transfer once. Hanging up or making Staff go and look is a fail.
behaved.rule: Ask ONCE, warmly, "oh gotcha, could you put me through to whoever handles the Pokemon?".

behaved.label: Reacted to a new person
behaved.why: Judged after a wait: Staff were away 27 seconds and may be the same person back, so nothing was expected of him.
behaved.tip: Only counts after a transfer, where whoever picks up never heard the question. A walk away is a maybe, and Charlie judges that one from the voice.
behaved.rule: When somebody new picks up, your recorded question plays again and you carry on from their answer.

behaved.label: Said goodbye when told no
behaved.why: Nobody ever said there was nobody to transfer to.
behaved.tip: Only counts when Staff said there was nobody to put us through to. Charlie must wrap up warmly and end, never keep pushing.
behaved.rule: When Staff say nothing is in stock, ask the restock question once, then thank them warmly and wrap up.

behaved.label: Meter stopped
behaved.why: The staff dropped Charlie, and the meter successfully stopped. Reconnected as part 3 of the same check.
behaved.tip: Charlie is dropped the moment Staff walk away or hand us on, so we stop paying, and comes back as a new part of the same check.
behaved.rule: The system holds the check while Staff are away; Charlie's meter stops for the wait.

behaved.label: Charlie wrapped up
behaved.why: Charlie thanked them and ended. They never gave a name.
behaved.tip: Charlie thanks them, by name when they gave one, and ends. A check that just stops leaves Staff talking to nobody.
behaved.rule: End the check with one warm goodbye in your own words, then end the check with end_call.

behaved.label: Spoke their language
behaved.why: No Spanish was spoken on this check.
behaved.tip: On a Spanish check Charlie speaks Spanish the whole way through. Answering in English on a Spanish check is a fail.
behaved.rule: If Staff speak Spanish, continue in Spanish.

behaved.label: Charlie ended the check
behaved.tip: Charlie finishing the conversation himself is the clean ending. Staff hanging up on us, or the check dropping, is not.
behaved.rule: Say goodbye once, then end the check with end_call. Never leave the store to hang up on us.

rows.label: Charlie on the meter

say.tail: It ran 24 on the record. The goal is 23.

rows.open: Talking, listening and waiting all count while Charlie is on the clock. On this check he spoke for 3 seconds, listened for 5 seconds, and waited for 16 seconds. After the check ended, our reader proved a voice on it was a recording the store played, so 4 seconds of his clock grade as waiting — the row under this one says why.

rows.label: The store's recording, graded as a wait

say.post: of that was the store's recording playing, so it grades as a wait.

rows.open: After the check ended, our reader proved that what sounded like Staff talking was really a recording the store played — the check log names the line. A recorded voice is the one sound the live ear can never refuse, so the hold was never caught during the check. The owner ruled these grade fairly after the fact: as if the hold had been caught when the store's recording started, with Charlie dropped 3 seconds in. The record itself, the real cost and what the customer paid are unchanged.

rows.label: Awake while the store had us on hold

say.post: while the store had us waiting.

rows.open: The store was playing music, an advert, or nothing at all, and Charlie's meter was running through it. Every one of these seconds is money spent on hearing a store's hold music. When the system recognises the wait he is dropped and this number is small; when it cannot, this is what it costs. It is the real measured number, never an adjusted one.

rows.label: Of that, waiting on a quiet line
rows.open: Nobody was saying anything for those seconds, and Charlie's meter was still running. A hold that did not switch him off, or a slow answer, is usually where this time goes.

rows.label: Charlie's answer gap, worst turn
rows.open: Staff finished talking and this is how long Charlie's reply took to start. That wait is Staff standing on a quiet line.

rows.label: Echo's handover gap

say.pre: Echo handed Charlie the words in

rows.open: Echo is the earpiece that writes down what Staff say. This is how long their words took to reach Charlie after their voice stopped.

rows.label: The announced hold drop gap
rows.open: Staff said they were stepping away, and this is how long Charlie's meter kept running before it switched off. The waiting after the switch cost nothing.

rows.label: Gross profit
rows.value: 71% on the record, graded 74% against the 56% floor

say.tail: It made 71 on the record; the difference is the recording's seconds. The floor is 56.

rows.open: The price of the check, minus what it cost to run, as a share of the price. The Check cost card below says where the money went. The graded percent prices the store's recording seconds out of Charlie's cost, per the owner's advert ruling; the real cost and the customer's charge are unchanged. This scene scripts a hold long enough to force the phone line's second billed minute, so the goal on a hold test is 11 cents on a 25 cent check.

test.name: Hold: music with advert
test.sub: Staff put us on hold with music that has a recorded advert in it, and Charlie dropped until a person came back.
test.info: This test proves that a recorded voice inside hold music never reaches Charlie. An advert is a voice, so no listening rule can refuse it. His ears are shut the moment the hold is recognised, Echo alone keeps writing down what is said, and he comes back only when a real person is talking to us again.
